_note: Hand-written hints that win over tools/zh_hints.py rules: 13 for frequent HSK 1 characters the rules leave awkward, then 24 for characters Make Me a Hanzi (MMAH, dictionary.txt at the pinned commit) gives no usable template (no etymology or an unknown part); where it has none the hint says so and any mnemonic is marked as one, then 8 (fb43) for characters that occur only inside compounds, restating their decomposition so the compound line can carry a breakdown (the part after the last ": " is the meaning, dropped there). Each states why the rule fails and the source it restates. Facts only, no invented etymology. "_meanings" overrides the per-character meaning shown for a character inside a multi-character unit (same reason and source fields): a bare character key is the default, a "compound:char" key (e.g. "服务员:服") wins for that compound only, so each character reads as it functions in that word; a suffix or particle is labelled as one, a bound morpheme as "(part of X)", a transliteration as "(sound ...)".
